problem: The spec's `.prose-legal` counter block (also 09-design-tokens.md:331-350) was never implemented and is in neither globals.css nor the built stylesheet — `counter-reset`/`counter-increment` appear 0 times in src/ and 0 times in out/_next/static/chunks/*.css. That is CORRECT: LegalPageTemplate.tsx:183-194 deliberately replaced CSS counters with literal `.legal-n` spans + `ol.lit` because clause numbering is alphanumeric and per-Part (B12.6, D23.3), 'which no <ol> can produce'. The risk is that the spec still says otherwise. Prose.tsx emits `[&_ol]:list-decimal`; if a later agent implements §505 as written, `.prose-legal ol { list-style:none }` at (0,2,1) and the decimal marker collide and produce exactly the double-marker failure ('1. (a) …') that the template's comment warns about.
fix: Amend 00-design-contract.md:505-509 and 09-design-tokens.md:331-350 to record that `.prose-legal` is superseded by LegalPageTemplate's hoisted `<style href="legal-page">` block, and that CSS counters must NOT be added. No code change. (Spec file — not mine to edit; flagging for the spec owner.)

problem: The JSDoc comment explaining why the md: step was dropped writes the class name literally: "`md:text-6xl` step: `md:` is banned (Rule 1)". Tailwind's oxide scanner does not strip comments, so the utility is emitted into production CSS: `.md\:text-6xl{font-size:var(--text-6xl);line-height:var(--tw-leading,var(--text-6xl--line-height))}`. check-design-contract.mjs strips comments before check 2, so it correctly reports no SOURCE violation — but the stronger claim, that no md:/xl:/2xl: utility exists in this product's CSS, is false. Four more dead utilities ship the same way from comments: -mx-2, invert, max-w-prose, min-h-screen.
fix: Reword the comment so the literal class string never appears, e.g. 'a 6xl step at md: is banned (Rule 1)'. Then md:text-6xl is not a candidate and the built CSS contains no banned breakpoint at all. Same treatment for the other four mentions if the dead bytes matter.

problem: .btn-base and .card-hover (globals.css:70 and :94) are emitted into the shipped stylesheet but referenced by no component — `grep -rn 'card-hover|btn-base' src --include='*.tsx' --include='*.ts'` returns rc=1 for both. .btn-base exists only as the head of the selector list that works around Tailwind 4.1.18 rejecting `@apply btn-base`, so the name itself is never needed; .card-hover is simply unused (only .card is, in ServicePageTemplate.tsx).
fix: Drop `.btn-base,` from the selector list at globals.css:70, leaving `.btn-primary, .btn-secondary { … }` — identical emitted CSS minus one dead selector. Delete the `.card-hover` block, or apply it where cards were meant to lift. (globals.css belongs to another package this wave — reporting, not editing.)

problem: The unresolved token {{VICTOR_FULL_NAME}} is emitted inside structured data, not just body copy: all four /insights/[slug]/ pages ship "author":{"@type":"Person","name":"{{VICTOR_FULL_NAME}}"}. D6 requires Article "with a real named author". This is a known BLOCKERS.md item, but its severity is understated in the gate note — a literal brace token inside a Person entity is ingested by Google as the author's name and is far harder to walk back than the same token in prose. Same class applies to {{FOUNDER_FULL_NAME}}, which the gate note already identifies as the same human under a second spelling.
fix: Owner is Victor, not an agent — do not invent the value. Escalate this specific instance in docs/plans/BLOCKERS.md as schema-level (blocks indexing correctness, not only copy), and unify {{VICTOR_FULL_NAME}} and {{FOUNDER_FULL_NAME}} into one token before resolution so the same string lands in src/data/insights/index.ts:52, /about/ and /imprint/.

problem: The 404 shell (out/404.html, out/404/index.html, out/_not-found/index.html — byte-identical) carries two <title> tags and two contradictory robots metas. Its own inline title plus Next's auto-injected `noindex` are joined by the root layout's defaults: `<title>IT Recruitment & Engineering Talent in Eastern Europe | TalentSync</title>`, `robots: index, follow`, the homepage description and the homepage og:title. not-found.tsx cannot export metadata (documented at src/app/not-found.tsx:17-22), so it cannot override them. Real-world impact is limited — Google takes the most restrictive robots and the first <title> — but nginx.conf:43 serves this file for every typo and dead backlink, and it currently presents itself as a second copy of the homepage. Note the canonical half of this trap is already correctly defused: the layout sets no `alternates`, so 404.html emits zero canonical tags.
fix: Move the homepage-specific values out of the layout default. In src/app/layout.tsx replace `title.default` and `description` with neutral site-level strings (or drop them, letting src/app/page.tsx's pageMeta supply the homepage copy it already sets via title.absolute), and remove `openGraph.title`, `openGraph.description` and `openGraph.url` — keep only metadataBase, openGraph.type/siteName/locale, twitter.card and icons. That leaves the 404 with one meaningful title and no homepage duplicate signal. While there: `title.template: '%s | TalentSync'` (line 26) contradicts 01-architecture.md:188 ("No title.template") and is inert anyway because pageMeta uses title.absolute — delete it.

problem: engagementModels is [] on line 367, so /tech-recruitment-eastern-europe/ carries neither BLOCK B nor BLOCK C, and / carries neither either. 02-page-content.md line 27 names exactly five pages that must carry them verbatim (/, tech-recruitment-eastern-europe, hire-software-developers-eastern-europe, b2b-engineer-recruitment, hourly-engineering-talent); only three of the five do, plus /about/ which is not on the list. problem: The homepage FAQ bypasses the 40-60 word discipline that every other FAQ on the site meets. problem: /hire-qa-engineers/ carries zero named placements (evidence: [], no 'Placements on record' section) and so fails the brief's requirement of one real named result - it is the only service page that does. The page handles this honestly rather than fabricating: 'our published placement record is in development roles. Nine engineers across five clients... and none of them was a QA or test-automation hire... it would be easy to let [Qualiwise] sit next to the word QA on this page and let you draw the wrong conclusion.' That is the correct call and it is why this is medium, not critical: draft: true is set in both the page and routes.ts:69, so it is noindexed and unlinked. It is also, at 2303 words, the shortest service page and the one 02-page-content already recommends cutting from launch.

Add a hard gate to assertServicePage so flipping draft to false without >=2 entries in evidence throws - the assertion currently only checks evidence >= 2 when draft is false, which is the right rule but should be accompanied by a comment on this page recording that the honest no-record section must be deleted at the same time the flip happens, or the page will contradict its own new evidence block.

problem: Six pages render under the brief's 800-word floor: /careers/ 377, /contact/ 499, /case-studies/silvertalent/ 662, /case-studies/qualiwise/ 698, /imprint/ 750, /case-studies/barca-mobile/ 755, /insights/ 757. problem: Line 322: <div className="mt-10 grid gap-10 lg:grid-cols-[16rem_minmax(0,65ch)] lg:items-start lg:gap-x-16"> declares grid columns ONLY at lg. Below lg the single implicit track is `auto`, whose minimum is the grid item's min-content. Prose gives every <table> `width:max-content` ([&_table]:w-max), so the widest table's max-content (measured 1870px on /terms/) becomes the article's min-content and the track blows out to the article's 65ch cap, 688.688px, inside a 321px container. Measured at 361x740: /terms/, /privacy/, /cookies/, /imprint/ all report documentElement.scrollWidth 704 vs clientWidth 353 — 351px of horizontal scroll, a direct Rule 4 violation on the two most important pages on the site. /candidate-privacy/, the only legal page with zero tables, has overflow 0, which isolates the cause. `[&_table]:overflow-x-auto` does not save it: the table's own width is max-content, so the article, not the table, is what overflows.
fix: Add a base-breakpoint track with a zero minimum to the wrapper: className="mt-10 grid grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)] gap-10 lg:grid-cols-[16rem_minmax(0,65ch)] lg:items-start lg:gap-x-16". Verified live in the page: gridTemplateColumns 688.688px -> 321px, documentElement.scrollWidth 704 -> 353, articleW 321, and the widest table then becomes its own scroller (scrollWidth 325 vs clientWidth 321).

problem: Line 291 carries the identical wrapper — "mt-10 grid gap-10 lg:grid-cols-[16rem_minmax(0,65ch)] lg:items-start lg:gap-x-16" — and the same bug. All four insights articles contain a table, and all four measure 351px of horizontal overflow at 361x740 (verified on /insights/moldova-it-park-single-tax-explained/: clientWidth 353, scrollWidth 704, gridTemplateColumns 688.688px). Eight of the 33 built routes scroll sideways on a phone.
fix: Same one-token change: add grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)] at the base breakpoint. Fix both files together — they are the same expression and will drift apart otherwise.

problem: Annex A is NOT reproduced inside /privacy/. out/privacy/#annex-a is an 836-byte pointer to /candidate-privacy/; the Art 14 phrases "Where we got your details", "What we recorded" and "disproportionate effort" return 0 hits on /privacy/ and 1 hit each on /candidate-privacy/. The spec's own justification for the annex is defeated by that: 03-privacy-policy.md says "It is reproduced here so you can check that what we sent you matches what we publish." A candidate who was sent the notice and opens the privacy policy to check it now has to follow a link. The single-canonical-text rationale is sound and is stated on the page, but this is a legal-drafting call, not a code call.
fix: Victor's decision. Either accept the pointer and amend the Annex A preamble so it no longer implies the text is reproduced there, or render the same LegalDoc block array in both places from one shared export so there is still one source of truth and two renderings. Do not hand-copy it.

problem: The comment on the table rules claims "the table is its own horizontal scroller (Rule 4)", but [&_table]:block [&_table]:w-max [&_table]:max-w-full does not produce that. width:max-content with max-width:100% makes the table compress and wrap rather than overflow-and-scroll. Measured on /terms/ after correcting the grid: all 3 tables render at exactly 321px and only one has any internal scroll (scrollWidth 325 vs clientWidth 321) — the other two squash their columns to fit 321px. /privacy/ carries 15 tables, including the five-column international-transfers table that is legally load-bearing, and they will squash hardest. It is also the max-content width that feeds the grid blow-out in the two critical findings above.
fix: Wrap the table instead of sizing it: render tables inside a <div class="overflow-x-auto"> in LegalPageTemplate's table branch and drop w-max/max-w-full/overflow-x-auto from Prose, so the table takes its natural width and the wrapper scrolls. That also removes the max-content contribution that breaks the grid. If squashing is preferred instead, keep the classes but delete the comment claiming it scrolls.

problem: Line 78's <a href="#cookie-settings"> is a dangling fragment in the static HTML on every page — it is the only broken in-page anchor found across all five legal pages (terms 102 unique fragments, 1 broken; same on the other four). problem: At 360x740 the banner measures 337.5px tall — 45.6% of the viewport — and reserves all of it as document.body padding-bottom (measured 338px).
